<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par159 />what the imperfect in the protasis had represented as still conceivable; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=12}}); with the perfect consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=5}}; with the protasis suppressed, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=8}} (see {{GHGpar|107|x}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|d}}
(''b'') {{GHGterm|Jussive}} in protasis (cf. {{GHGpar|109|h}}, i) and apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּֽשֶׁת־ח֫שֶׁךְ וִיהִי לָ֑יְלָה}} (if) ''thou makest darkness, it is night''; imperfect in the apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=29}}<sup> ''b''</sup>; cohortative {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=23}}. Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=7|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי לְתַנִּין|translate=it shall become a serpent}}, is the apodosis to a suppressed protasis ''if thou cast it down''; so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=וְיָשֹׁב}} is the apodosis to a protasis ''if thou wash'', contained in what precedes.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|e}}
(''c'') ''Cohortative'' (see {{GHGpar|108|e}}) in the protasis; perfect in the apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=6}}; imperfect consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=אָק֫וּמָה וַיְרַבְּרוּ־בִי}} (if) ''I arise, they speak against me''; on the cohortative in the apodosis, cf. {{GHGpar|108|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|f}}
(''d'') {{GHGterm|Imperfect consecutive}} in the protasis ({{GHGpar|111|x}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=וָאֹֽמַד|translate=if I say}}, &c. (with a noun-clause as the apodosis); with a frequentative perfect consecutive in the apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=16}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|g}}
(''e'') {{GHGterm|Perfect consecutive}} in the protasis and apodosis (see the examples, {{GHGpar|112|kk}} and ll), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=וְעָוַב אָבִיו וָמֵת|translate=and should he leave his father, his father would die}}; 9:15, 44:29, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=30}}; with frequentative perfects, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=21}} (referring to the past, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=20|verse=9}}); with imperfect in the apodosis (being separated from the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} by {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=24}}; introduced by an infinitive absolute, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=37}}; an interrogative clause in the apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=10|verse=19}}; a noun-clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=21}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|h}}
(''f'') ''A simple perfect'' (to represent actions which are to be regarded as completed) in the protasis and apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=18|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=מָצָא אִשָּׁה מָצָא טוֹב|translate=has one found a wife, he has found a good thing}}; an imperfect in the apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=10|hidebook=1}}; an imperfect consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=13|hidebook=1}}<sup> ''b''</sup>, 29:11; an interrogative clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=12|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=20}} ''if I have sinned'' (prop., well, now I have sinned!) ''what can I do unto thee?'' 21:31, 35:6, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=3|verse=8}}; a noun-clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=19}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|i}}
(''g'') ''A participle as casus pendens'' (cf. {{GHGpar|143|d}}, and the sections of the Grammar there cited, esp. {{GHGpar|116|w}}) or a complete noun-clause in the protasis; the apodosis mostly introduced by {{GHGterm|wāw apodosis}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=24}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} {{GHGheb|text=יוֹלֵד חָכָם וְיִשְׂמַח בּוֹ|translate=if one begetteth a wise child, he shall have joy of him}}; with perfect frequentative in the apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=13}}, &c.; but also with a simple imperfect, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=12}} (cf. {{GHGpar|112|n}}); with an interrogative imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=2}}, 19; with an interrogative perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=13}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|k}}
(''h'') ''Infinitive with preposition'' (also as the equivalent of a conditional clause) in the protasis, and a perfect consecutive in the apodosis (cf. {{GHGpar|112|mm}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=7|verse=14}} ff. {{GHGheb|text=בְּהַֽעֲוֹתוֹ וֽהֹֽכַחְתִּיו וג׳|translate=if he commit iniquity, I will correct him}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=34}} f. (with imperfect, followed by perfects frequentative in the apodosis).

Rem. On the expression of condition and consequence by means of two co-ordinate ''imperatives'', see {{GHGpar|110|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|l}}
'''3.''' Particles used to introduce conditional sentences are {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} (for which in the later and latest Books sometimes {{GHGheb|text=הֵן}}, see below, under w) and {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}}<ref>On {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} cf. Kohler in Geiger’s ''Zeitschr. für Wiss. und Leben'', vi (1868), p. 21 ff.</ref> ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=לוּא}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=6|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=7|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=אִלּוּ}}, from {{GHGheb|text=אִם לוּ}}) ''if'', negative {{GHGheb|text=אִם לֹא}} and {{GHGheb|text=לוּלֵא}} ({{GHGheb|text=לוּלֵי}}) ''unless''; {{GHGheb|text=כִּי|translate=supposing that}} (Lat. ''ut''), ''in case that'', sometimes used almost in the same sense as {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}. With regard to the difference between {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} ({{GHGheb|text=אִם לֹא}}) and {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} ({{GHGheb|text=לוּלֵא}}), the fundamental rule is that {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} is used if the condition be regarded either as already fulfilled, or if it, together with its consequence, be thought of as possibly (or<section end=par159 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
